newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court reaffirms block on power station plans.
newsitem.headline: Turk court reaffirms block on power station plans.

text.p: Turkey's top administrative court on Thursday reiterated its decision to halt the implementation of the build-operate (BO) system for thermal power stations in a blow to the government's plans to close growing energy deficits.
State-run Anatolian news agency said the general assembly of the Council of State was ruling on an Energy Ministry objection to a previous decision to stop the system being used.
The decision will effect several gas- and coal-fired power plant projects worth more than $1 billion.
"The general council, approving the decision to stop the implementation, rejected the objection," Anatolian said.
The Energy Ministry had received bids from several local and international companies for six such plants after the court's previous decision, Anatolian said.

The court still has to rule on whether to make the order to halt the BO system permanent. The system was devised last year only for thermal power plants to overcome legal obstacles encountered by its parent model, build-operate-transfer (BOT).

The older BOT model, devised in the 1980s to finance big infrastructure projects through foreign-led consortia, previously hit bureaucratic snags after court rulings that their finances should be inspected by the Council of State.
The BO system is an important part of Energy Ministry plans to help offset an energy deficit which is expected to reach 2.5 billion kilowatt hours (kWh) in 1997.

Turkey, whose energy demand rose 12 percent in 1996 and is forecast to continuing rising sharply into the next century, began importing power from Iran, Georgia and Bulgaria late last year to make up the energy shortfall.
